newsitem.title: LEBANON: SOLIDERE fell in the last week on BSM.
newsitem.headline: SOLIDERE fell in the last week on BSM.

text.p: SOLIDERE fell in the last week of trade ended on Friday on the Beirut Secondary Market (BSM) in profit-taking which followed a two-week surge on the privately-operated market.
The shares will begin trading on the official Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, adding some $2 billion to the BSE capitalisation currently calculated at less than $400 million.
Weekly turnover on the BSM fell sharply to 25,140 shares from 75,134 last week and value was $2,828,651 from $8,634,534.
A shares, distributed to former holders of property rights in the central Beirut disctrict SOLIDERE is rebuilding, fell to $112.5 from last Friday's $115.625.
B shares, issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994, fell to $113 from $117.50.
"It was a period of profit-taking," one dealer told Reuters. "I expect quiet trade in a wait-and-see period on the first few days of trade on the official bourse," he added.
The shares had begun a rally three weeks ago after expectations that SOLIDERE will launch a $150 million GDR issue in October allowing non-Arab investors access to the market.
On the BSE, only 5,530 Eternit shares were traded on Wednesday at $1.875 down from $1.9375 on September 16.
There was no trade in any of the other three listed companies throughout the week: Ciments Libanais, Ciments Blancs, and Uniceramic.
The Lebanon Invest Share Price Index (LISPI) fell 1.64 percent on the week to 83.74 and the BLOM Stock Index (BSI) fell 3.14 to 964.3. Both indexes cover both markets.
